# Area-Based Names & Latch Mode

New holds are named after their area, so their entity IDs are short and predictable. Every hold now gets its own device.

### Changed
- **Holds are named after their area.** Leave the name blank and a hold is named after its area, e.g. **Ensuite**, giving `binary_sensor.ensuite_occupancy`, `binary_sensor.ensuite_latch`, `sensor.ensuite_hold_ends`, `number.ensuite_hold_time`, `select.ensuite_latch_mode`, `switch.ensuite_force_occupied` and `button.ensuite_release_latch`. A single-sensor hold uses the sensor's area, or the sensor's name if it has no area.
- **Latch trigger is now called Latch mode.** Same entity and options; only the name has changed.
- **Every hold has its own device.** The *Add to the sensor's device* option has been removed. On current Home Assistant versions it created a separate device named "Hold & Latch", which gave its entities IDs like `binary_sensor.hold_latch_hold`.

### Upgrade notes
- **Holds added to their sensor's device** move to a device of their own, named after the hold. The sensor's own device is left as it was.
- **Existing entity IDs don't change.** Home Assistant keeps an entity's ID once it's created. To get the new IDs, delete the hold and add it again with the name left blank. For holds that had their own device, renaming the device to the area name and accepting Home Assistant's offer to update the entity IDs also works.
- Update any automations, scripts or dashboards that use the old entity IDs.
- Update from **Settings → Updates**, then restart Home Assistant.

**Full Changelog**: https://github.com/sambarlick/Hold-Latch/compare/v0.8.0...v0.9.0
